- 2026-11-08: Finished Progress Report 9, "Preliminary results." Created `04-results.qmd` (with `execute: cache: false`, as required) reporting the main finding with every number computed inline from the data rather than typed: across 82 of 85 tracts with both estimates, income significantly predicts rent (coefficient $0.0047, R² = 19.4%), and the spatial error model's error term is itself significant (λ = 0.381), confirming the spatial clustering found in Progress Report 8. Added a results table (@tbl-regression) and a results map (@fig-rent-map) with a real scale bar, a titled legend, a named classification scheme, and missing tracts shown rather than hidden — the map requirement this time was stricter than earlier weeks' "scale or stated extent." Added a spatial checks table reporting the actual estimate under each pitfall named in the proposal. Kept observation separate from interpretation: this chapter states only what the data and models show, and I moved my actual thinking about what the income-rent relationship might mean into `notes/2026-11-08-interpretation.md`, dated, to develop later once Lecture 10 (discussion and conclusions) is covered. Also fixed `_quarto.yml`'s commented-out `appendices:` line, flagged in the PR7 feedback, so the Markdown practice file no longer shows as a numbered chapter. I used Claude Code to help me with the regression/Moran's I code (reused from PR8). Claude also assisted in building the scale-bar map, which needed I realized needed a new package (`matplotlib-scalebar`) I hadn't used before.

- 2026-11-01: Completed Progress Report 8, "Data analysis." Updated `03-model.qmd` to use the cleaned analysis dataset (`albany-analysis.gpkg`) instead of the old downloaded files. Added an analysis plan before running the analysis. Explored the data and found that 83 out of 85 census tracts had both rent and income estimates. Created rent maps using two classification methods (Quantiles and Natural Breaks) to show how different methods affect map appearance. Built Queen Contiguity and K-Nearest Neighbors (k=4) spatial weights using 82 complete tracts. Ran Global and Local Moran's I tests and found significant spatial autocorrelation in rent values, although only 2 tracts remained significant after correction. Ran an OLS regression to examine the relationship between rent and income. Income was statistically significant, and the model explained 19% of the variation in rent (R² = 0.19). Conducted Lagrange Multiplier tests, which produced mixed results, so I reported the uncertainty rather than forcing a conclusion. Fitted a Spatial Error Model, which confirmed a significant spatial error effect while maintaining the basic relationship between income and rent. Added a Spatial Checks section to test the two potential issues identified in my proposal. Also corrected the coefficient of variation calculation based on my professor's feedback. Used Claude Code to troubleshoot spatial-analysis libraries, correct API usage, and identify and fix a missing code-block closure that was affecting the final output.
